title: Francis Xavier (1506–1552)
hook: he baptizes across India and Japan and dies off the coast of China

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Jesuits: a failed pilgrimage, an offer to the pope, and a motto. Your line was for the greater glory. Today one of Ignatius's roommates is sent east.

The ending comes first. A small island off the coast of China, a hut, a fever, and a man waiting for a boat that never comes. He plans to slip into the mainland, where foreigners are forbidden, and he's been told it could cost him his freedom or his life. He's still waiting when he dies. Behind him lie India, the islands of the spice trade, and Japan. He was once a promising young teacher in Paris, rooming with an older student who kept asking him an uncomfortable question. The older student was Ignatius. The young teacher was Francis Xavier.
screen: `AN ISLAND OFF CHINA.` → `A BOAT THAT NEVER COMES.` → `ONCE A TEACHER IN PARIS.`

segments.voice: Tradition says Ignatius kept repeating one line of the Gospel to his ambitious roommate, from Matthew, in the Douay-Rheims: "For what doth it profit a man, if he gain the whole world, and suffer the loss of his own soul?" Xavier wanted a career. That question slowly turned him around. Then, the sending. When the king of Portugal asked for missionaries for India, another Jesuit was chosen and fell ill. Xavier was sent instead, almost overnight. He never saw Ignatius again. Then, the road. In India he walked the coast, taught children prayers in their own language, and baptized. He went on to the islands, and to Japan, where he learned that his ragged clothes made people take him less seriously, not more, and changed his approach. Then China, whose mainland he never reached. All along, Xavier wrote long letters home to his brothers in Europe, and they were copied and read aloud. In one he wishes he could run through the universities of Europe shouting to the students about the people waiting for someone to come. It's also true that his travels went by Portuguese ships, inside a trading empire, and that empire's record is a hard one. The Church names him a patron of the missions. His line, if he had one, was always further.
screen: `WHAT DOTH IT PROFIT A MAN?` · `SENT IN ANOTHER MAN'S PLACE.` · `INDIA, THE ISLANDS, JAPAN.` · `LETTERS READ ALOUD IN EUROPE.` · then, large: `ALWAYS FURTHER.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone far from you, in another city, another country, or just far in the ways that count, and picture their face. Ask what they'd be glad to hear from you, and let a few lines take shape in your mind. If you pray, pray for them as the words come; if you don't, simply keep them in mind.
Francis Xavier. Ignatius's roommate from Paris, sent east to India and Japan, who died on an island off the coast of China, still going further.
Your line: always further. One more step past where you'd usually stop. Day eight hundred fifty, done.

howItsDone: Catholics keep Francis Xavier's feast, and he is honored as a patron of missions; his remains are venerated in Goa, India.

chat.says: Who was Francis Xavier? Is he the same as Saint Francis?
options: No, a different Francis: Ignatius's Paris roommate, a Jesuit sent to India and Japan.
Yes. Francis Xavier is Saint Francis of Assisi's full name, as used in Spain.
No. He was the Portuguese king who sent the first missionaries to India.
chat.meaning: Francis Xavier was Ignatius's roommate in Paris, sent east to India, the islands and Japan; he died off China, still going further.
